title: Hybrid cluster fleet strategy and upgrade notes
content:
Purpose and context:

This note collects strategy, constraints, and a minimally actionable upgrade/maintenance approach for hybrid on-prem Kubernetes fleets consisting of vSphere VMs and bare-metal nodes. Goal is to converge provisioning, lifecycle, and upgrade practices so customer private deployments behave predictably and we can reuse Terraform modules and runbooks across both substrate types.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Terraform module responsibilities and layout for hybrid fleets
- Day-2 upgrade plan (kube, CSI, CNI, OS, firmware) with canary approach
- Validation checks / smoke tests and metrics to verify health post-upgrade
- Network, storage and BMC operational notes special to vSphere vs bare metal
- Known risks and rollback primitives

Non-goals:
- Deep dives into installer choices (kOps/kubeadm/Tinkerbell) - we assume a curated installer per customer
- Full CI automation (this is runbook/design, automation tracked in GHPRs linked above)

Assumptions and constraints:
- Clusters run mixed node pools: vmPool (vSphere VMs) and metalPool (bare metal). Both present to the same control plane.
- Image registry may be air-gapped for some customers; repo mirroring step is part of onboarding.
- We maintain a private control plane (managed by customer or Redwood Private control plane depending on engagement).

Terraform module layout (high level):
- modules/network: VLAN and subnet allocation, load balancer VIPs, NSX/vSphere network tags optional
- modules/compute/vsphere: vm templates, customization spec, OVA import glue, affinity rules
- modules/compute/baremetal: BMC/IPMI provisioning, iPXE templates, ignition/kickstart artifacts storage
- modules/storage: vSphere CSI policy objects + Ceph/Rook/Longhorn overlays for metal
- modules/cluster: kubeadm/Tinkerbell invocation, CA certs lifecycle, kubelet config, kubeadm join tokens
- modules/ops: metrics exporter config, node-exporter, alertmanager routing, drain helpers

Notes on module design choices:
- Keep compute modules idempotent and declarative: modules should not perform ad-hoc provisioning actions during plan/apply without a clear safety gate (e.g. apply with var.execute = true).
- Expose a minimal interface: node labels, taints, machineType (vm|metal), and lifecycle policies. Avoid shipping provider-specific knobs into cluster consumers.
- Use a shared secrets backend (Vault/KMS). Terraform should read secrets for cloud init but not store credentials in state.

Upgrade plan (high level steps):
1) Pre-flight and snapshot phase
   - Ensure last successful backups for etcd (if managed in-cluster) or control plane snapshot exists.
   - Snapshot vSphere templates and take hardware config snapshot notes for metal nodes (BIOS config file export if available).
   - Run terraform plan against modules to detect drift.

2) Canary pool (non-critical workload) creation
   - Create a small canary node pool on target substrate (both vmPool and metalPool separately to validate substrate differences).
   - Deploy benchmark app + synthetic workload to exercise scheduling, CSI mounts, and network egress.

3) Control plane upgrade (if applicable)
   - If control plane is in-cluster and multi-master, follow control-plane rolling upgrade: cordon -> evict non-critical pods -> upgrade kubelet/kubeadm on a single master -> verify control plane health -> proceed next master.
   - If control plane is managed external to cluster (Redwood Private control plane), coordinate maintenance window and failover steps with SRE.

4) Node pool upgrades (parallelizable across pools with care)
   - For vmPool (vSphere): create a replacement VM from the new template and join cluster; drain and retire old node once new node is healthy.
   - For metalPool: PXE reprovision with updated OS image / kubelet config; if reprovisioning is not available, perform in-place package upgrades followed by kubelet restart and health checks.
   - Always prefer add-replace pattern where substrate allows it (vSphere templates make this easier).

5) Post-upgrade validation
   - Automated smoke tests: kube-api responsiveness (kubectl get nodes), DNS resolution (curl to cluster dns svc), CSI mount test, PV IO test (fio), LB e2e (ingress HTTP 200), metrics ingestion.
   - Canary load test (short synthetic traffic burst) and latency/cpu spike observation.

6) Rollback primitives
   - For vmPool: power off new nodes and re-add old template VMs. Keep old templates for at least one release cycle.
   - For metalPool: if reprovisioning fails, use image based rollback (boot from previous image) or replace node from spare metal nodes if available.
   - Restore etcd snapshot if control plane is unhealthy and all masters are impacted.

Substrate specifics and warnings:
- vSphere notes:
  - Use vSphere tags to track nodePool membership; make sure automation respects DRS/HA policies.
  - Ghost NIC MAC changes when cloning templates can break DHCP reservations; prefer customization spec and static MAC mapping if customer relies on MAC tracking.
  - vSphere CSI takes time to reconcile PVs when provider versions change - add a PV migration/verification window in the runbook.

- Bare metal notes:
  - Ensure iPXE/TTFTP images are signed; chain of trust required for regulated customers.
  - Local PVs require clear eviction semantics. Prefer PVCs on distributed storage (Ceph/Longhorn) for HA workloads.
  - Firmware upgrades MUST be decoupled from kube upgrades. Schedule firmware separately and validate node health afterwards.

Networking and CNI considerations:
- Standardize on a single CNI across the fleet where possible (Calico preferred for policy + BGP in metal; on vSphere use overlay mode or BGP depending on L2 topology).
- MetalLB for bare metal load balancing; keep an IP address pool per datacenter/cluster.
- If NSX/NSX-T in customer environment, map logical segments to Terraform network module outputs and avoid dynamic reallocation during upgrades.

Observability and SLO checkpoints:
- Before upgrade capture baseline: p50/p95 latency for API, token cost per op, pod start time distribution, control plane CPU.
- Post-upgrade target: no regressions > 2x baseline at p95 for non-peak traffic; any regression triggers immediate halt and investigation.

Testing and smoke test checklist (automated where possible):
- kubectl get componentstatuses and core DNS tests
- create namespace, deploy indexer pod with attached PVC, run fio (write 100Mi, verify checksum)
- simulate node failure: cordon + drain + kill kubelet; verify automatic rescheduling and PV detach/attach
- cpu/mem soak for 5m at low level workloads; observe OOM/kubelet restarts

Known risks and open questions (action items):
- How to expose a unified TTL for kubeadm join tokens across substrates? (PR in infra repo)
- Edge sites with intermittent BMC: need a different reprovisioning approach - explore disk swap + reimaging instead of PXE for edge.
- Longhorn vs Rook decision matrix: create an internal matrix that maps recovery time objectives to storage choices per customer.
- Airgap image signing and provenance enforcement: finalize tooling for image mirroring and attestations.

Immediate TODOs (next 2 weeks):
- Evan: prototype terraform module flag var.execute gating for compute modules (GHPR opened).
- Aisha: write metal reprovisioning iPXE snippets with signed images; add to modules/compute/baremetal.
- Jonah: run a mock upgrade test on staging cluster (one vmPool + one metalPool) and record metrics to S3 bucket infra-upgrade-artifacts.

Appendix: quick commands and checks
- Verify node readiness: kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep Ready
- CSI basic test: kubectl apply -f tests/csi-smoke.yaml && kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod -l app=csi-smoke --timeout=120s
- Drain helper (safest): kubectl drain NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force

Unresolved notes to convert into issues:
- Document exact template naming scheme for vSphere templates (standardized tags + version suffix).
- Add terraform state locking/retention guidelines for air-gapped customers.

End of draft - feedback welcome. This is intentionally operational and lower-level than the fleet policy doc; aim to convert the TODOs into GH tickets and a concise single-page runbook once we validate the staging canary results.
